pages.text: The disc's spin collapses suddenly. It happens when the stabilizers snap back at high spin, or a stabilizer runs out of mass while spinning.$(br2)The trapped energy dumps into the core and a $(num)60 second$() timer starts.
pages.title: Disc Stall

pages.text: Go round all four stabilizers and throw each $(item)Breaker Panel$() to $(warn)OVERCHARGED$(). Then press $(thing)Jump$() on the control console: the stabilizers kick the disc back into spin and the breakers drop back to normal.$(br2)Pressing Jump too early costs $(num)5$() seconds. If the timer runs out: $(danger)pre-meltdown$().
pages.title: Recovering a stall

pages.text: Spinning above $(num)4,000 rpm$() builds ring stress. Set a negative offset to brake the disc (or a positive one if it's spinning backwards), or $(thing)Shut Down$().$(br2)At $(num)100%$() the ring fails: $(danger)pre-meltdown$().
pages.title: Overspin

pages.text: Below $(num)10,000$() total mass, stability drops. Refuel or shut down.$(br2)Below $(num)4,000$() the core can't be held: $(danger)pre-meltdown$().
pages.title: Mass Starvation

pages.text: Breaking any part of the structure while the reactor runs sends it straight to $(danger)pre-meltdown$().$(br2)Put the block back fast.
pages.title: Containment Breach
One on top of another
pages.text: Failures stack. If a new one hits while you're dealing with another (a breach during a fault, a stall during pre-meltdown), the first is $(thing)put on hold$(), its timer paused, and comes back exactly as it was once the new one is handled. The console shows what's waiting: $(thing)Then: ...$()$(br2)A failure that runs out of time stays underneath with half its time back. Only a vent or a meltdown clears them all.
